## Privacy Policy

Effective Date: October 22, 2026

01. ### INTRODUCTION.


    This Privacy Policy (the “Policy”) explains how WindBorne Systems Inc. (“WindBorne”) collects, uses, and discloses personal information through windbornesystems.com (the “Site”), the WindBorne Data Viewer (the “Data Viewer”), and WindBorne weather tools and applications made available through third-party artificial intelligence services (the “AI Weather Tools” and, collectively with the Site and Data Viewer, the “Services”). For purposes of this Policy, the “Services” also include any other websites, products, services, applications, or tools that WindBorne offers through or under the Site, including its subdomains, whether or not an account is required. WindBorne may provide an additional or different privacy notice for a particular Service. That notice will control with respect to the processing it specifically addresses, and this Policy will otherwise continue to apply unless that notice expressly states that it applies in place of this Policy. In this Policy, the “marketing website” means our public informational pages, including our product information, articles, contact forms, and community pages. References to the marketing website do not describe all processing carried out by the Data Viewer, AI Weather Tools, or other account-based products. This Policy applies when you access or use the Services and when you otherwise interact with WindBorne, such as when you contact us.

02. ### INFORMATION COLLECTED AND HOW WE USE IT.


    As explained further in this section, you will have the opportunity to provide us with certain personal information. In addition, we may collect certain information automatically through your use of the Services and receive information from third-party services through which you access the Services. We will use this information to provide you with the functionality of our Services, to improve our Services, and to provide you with information about our Services. The rest of this section provides a more detailed explanation of the personal information we collect, the basis for our collection, and how we use that information. Depending on the purpose, where applicable law requires a legal basis for processing, we rely on performance of a contract, compliance with legal obligations, your consent, or our legitimate interests in providing, securing, maintaining, and improving the Services and communicating with you, as described in this Policy.




    1. **Voluntarily Disclosed Information.**



       1. **Account Creation.** If a Service permits or requires an account, we may ask you to provide your email address and other information needed to establish and manage your account. You may also be required to choose a password. We use this information so that we can provide and administer the applicable Service and otherwise perform our contract with you. We may also use your email address to send you promotional communications where permitted by law. You may opt out of promotional communications at any time by using the unsubscribe link in the message or contacting us.

       2. **Contacting Us and Website Requests.** When you contact us or submit a balloon recovery report or community launch request, we collect the information you provide. Depending on the form, this may include your name, email address, organization, product interests, how you heard about us, message, balloon identification number, shipping address, LinkedIn profile URL, launch purpose, or requested city and state. We also receive any other information you choose to include in your correspondence. We use this information to respond to inquiries, coordinate balloon recovery and community launches, and protect our forms against spam and abuse. Fields marked as required are needed to process a request through that form; other fields are optional. Where applicable law requires a legal basis, we rely on our legitimate interests in responding to requests and operating these activities, or on taking steps at your request before entering into a contract, as appropriate. We may also use your email address to send you promotional communications where permitted by law. You may opt out of promotional communications at any time by using the unsubscribe link in the message or contacting us.


    2. **Information Received from Third-Party Services.**



       1. **AI Weather Tool Requests.** When you use an AI Weather Tool through a third-party artificial intelligence service, we receive the task-specific information that the service sends to fulfill your request. Depending on the request, this may include a place name or address, geographic coordinates or other location information, locale, time zone, requested dates or times, weather variables, activity information, comparison locations, and related portions of your request. That information may be provided by you, inferred from your request, or supplied by the third-party service based on your settings or permissions. We use this information to provide, secure, maintain, monitor, and troubleshoot the AI Weather Tools, comply with law, and improve the Services. Requested or derived location information and the time of a request may also be recorded in technical logs. The AI Weather Tools are designed to receive only the information needed for the tool request, not your full conversation with the third-party service.


    3. **Automatically Collected Information.**



       1. **Browser & Device Information.** When you interact with the Services, we and our service providers may receive technical information from your browser or device, including your IP address, browser and device type, access times, requested pages or features, and performance or error information. The information collected depends on the Service and features you use. Account-based products and other Services may also use cookies, device or session identifiers, and location information as described in this Policy. Website form submissions include the submission page and, when available, referring-page and campaign information. We use this information to operate and secure the Services, prevent abuse, troubleshoot problems, understand how people find us, and improve the Services. You can learn more about cookies and related technologies in our [Cookie Policy](https://windbornesystems.com/ext/legal#cookie-policy). Where applicable, we rely on our legitimate interests in operating, securing, and improving the Services, performance of a contract, or consent where required. In connection with AI Weather Tools, we may also collect timestamps, platform and tool usage, control interactions, locale, requested or derived location information, browser or device information, performance and error data, and pseudonymous user or session identifiers that do not directly include your name or contact information. We use this information to count users, understand usage by country and time of day, identify common usage patterns, monitor and troubleshoot the Services, and improve the AI Weather Tools.

       2. **Emails.** We may receive a confirmation when you open an email from us.


03. ### DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION.


    We may disclose your personal information to the categories of third parties identified in this section.



    1. **Personnel and Third Party Service Providers.** We employ personnel and engage other companies and people to perform tasks on our behalf and need to share your personal information with them to provide products or services to you. For example, these providers may provide hosting and infrastructure, technical logging and monitoring, analytics, security, geocoding and weather data, communications, and other services needed to operate the Services. When you use an AI Weather Tool, the third-party artificial intelligence service sends task-specific information to WindBorne and receives WindBorne’s response. That service separately processes your information under its own privacy policy.


       **Website form processing.** We use Formspree to process and store contact inquiries and community-launch requests and deliver them to our team by email. Balloon recovery reports are submitted directly to our internal operations systems for our recovery team to handle. Submissions are available to personnel handling the request and to service providers supporting form delivery and email. Formspree may process technical information, such as IP addresses, browser information, access times, and referring pages, to operate its service and prevent spam and abuse. See [Formspree’s Privacy Policy](https://formspree.io/legal/privacy-policy/).

    2. **Analytics Services.** We use Google Analytics to understand how visitors engage with our Services. You can learn more about the information that Google has access to at [Google’s information about partner sites and apps](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites). We also use PostHog and may use other analytics and monitoring providers to process timestamps, platform and tool usage, control interactions, locale and location information, browser or device information, pseudonymous user or session identifiers, and performance and error data on our behalf for analytics, monitoring, troubleshooting, and service improvement. On the marketing website, we use Google Analytics after you accept optional analytics to measure page visits, engagement, and successful contact inquiries, community launch requests, and beta signups. We do not use PostHog on the marketing website. We do not send form contents, names, or email addresses to Google Analytics, and we remove URL query strings and fragments from page addresses sent for analytics. Separately, we may send validated campaign labels identifying a source, medium, campaign, or individual marketing link. These labels must not contain personal information. Advertising personalization and Google Signals are disabled. You can change your choice using the [Change cookie preferences](https://windbornesystems.com/ext/legal#cookie-policy) option in our Cookie Policy below.

    3. **Embedded Media and Social Content.** Some pages include video, audio, or social content provided by third parties, such as YouTube, Vimeo, LinkedIn, SoundCloud, or CBS News. Where an “Allow and load” notice appears, we do not load that embedded content until you choose to enable it. Loading it connects your browser to the provider, which receives your IP address and may use cookies or similar technologies for content delivery, analytics, or advertising. The notice links to the provider’s privacy policy. Your choice applies to that individual embed. You can select “Unload” to remove it from the page; this does not delete information already received by the provider or cookies it has stored. External links take you to services governed by their own privacy practices.

    4. **Events and Luma.** Our Get Involved page includes an event calendar provided by Luma. The calendar loads automatically and connects your browser to Luma when displayed. Luma may receive technical information, including your IP address and browser information, and may use cookies and analytics technologies. If you register for an event through Luma, Luma processes your registration information and shares information with the event host. When WindBorne hosts the event, we use the registration information we receive to organize the event and communicate with attendees. Where a legal basis is required, we rely on our legitimate interests in administering events, taking steps at your request or performing a contract where applicable, and consent where required. See [Luma’s Privacy Policy](https://luma.com/privacy-policy).

    5. **Anonymous Information.** We may provide aggregate usage information to third parties (or allow these third parties to collect aggregate information of activity on our Services), who may use that information to understand how often and in what ways people use our Services, so that they, too, can provide our users with an optimal online experience.

    6. **Business Transfers.** If we (or our assets) are acquired, or if we go out of business, enter bankruptcy, or go through some other change of control, personal information could be one of the assets transferred to or acquired by a third party.

    7. **Legal Compliance.** We reserve the right to access, read, preserve, and disclose any information that we believe is necessary to comply with governmental requests, law enforcement or court orders, or enforce or apply our [Terms of Service](https://windbornesystems.com/ext/legal#terms-of-service) and other agreements.


04. ### SECURITY.


    We use commercially reasonable physical, managerial, and technical safeguards to preserve the integrity and security of your personal information. In addition, we rely on the technical safeguards provided by the third party service providers we use to host, store, and process your personal information. We cannot, however, ensure or warrant that your personal information may not be accessed, disclosed, altered, or destroyed by breach of any of our physical, technical, or managerial safeguards. We are not responsible to our users or to any third party due to any such loss, misuse, or alteration.

05. ### YOUR RIGHTS.




    1. **How to Exercise Your Rights.** Depending on where you live, you may have rights under data protection laws in relation to your personal information. We will respond to requests, including appeals where applicable, as required by law. You can learn more about your rights further down in this section. If we have collected your personal information as a result of our relationship with you, we are a “controller” of that personal information and you can exercise your rights with respect to your personal information by following the instructions below. However, if we process your personal information on behalf of your employer or another organization through which you use a Service (your “Organization”) under an agreement that covers that Service (the “Organization Agreement”), we are a “processor” of your personal information and your Organization controls our use of your personal information and determines how and for what purpose we process your personal information. WindBorne remains the controller of information it handles for its own purposes, including information associated with your use of Services outside the Organization Agreement.


       If we process your personal information on behalf of your Organization under an Organization Agreement, and you have any questions or concerns about how your personal information is handled or would like to exercise your rights as a data subject, you should contact your Organization. If your request also concerns information for which WindBorne is the controller, WindBorne will respond directly to that portion of the request. We will provide assistance to the Organization to address any concerns you may have, in accordance with the Organization Agreement and applicable law.

    2. **Additional Information for European Economic Area (“EEA”) and United Kingdom (“UK”) Users.** If you reside in the EEA or the UK and we are a controller of your personal information, you have the following rights: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection authority in the country where you live or work or where you believe a violation occurred.




       1. **Request access to your personal information.** You may request a copy of the personal information we hold about you and to check that we are lawfully processing it. Where we have good reason, and where data protection law permits, we can refuse your request for a copy of your personal information, or certain elements of the request. If we refuse your request or any element of it, we will provide you with our reason(s) for doing so.

       2. **Request correction of your personal information.** You may request that we correct any incomplete or inaccurate data we hold about you.

       3. You may request that we delete or remove personal information where there is no good reason for us continuing to process it. You may also ask us to delete or remove your personal information where you have successfully exercised your right to object to processing (see below), where we may have processed your personal information unlawfully or where we are required to erase your personal information to comply with local law. Note, however, that we may not always be able to comply with your request of erasure for specific legal reasons which will be notified to you, if applicable, at the time of your request. You may not request the removal of de-identified, anonymous, or aggregate data from our databases.

       4. **Right to Object to or Restrict Processing.** In certain circumstances, you have the right to object to our processing of your personal information (for example, if we are processing your personal information on the basis of our legitimate interests but there are no longer any compelling legitimate grounds to justify our processing overriding your rights and interests). You may also restrict our processing of your personal information, for example during a period in which we are verifying the accuracy of your personal information in circumstances where you have challenged the accuracy of that personal information.

       5. **Request the transfer of your personal information to you or to a third party.** In certain instances, you have a right to receive the personal information that we hold about you (or a portion thereof) in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format. In such circumstances, you can ask us to transmit your personal information to you or directly to a third-party organization on your behalf. While we are happy for such requests to be made, we are not able to guarantee technical compatibility with a third-party organization’s systems. We are also unable to comply with requests that relate to personal information of others without their consent.

       6. **Withdraw consent.** You may withdraw your consent for our processing of your personal information where we are relying on consent to process that personal information. However, this will not affect the lawfulness of any processing carried out before you withdraw your consent. If you withdraw your consent, we may not be able to provide certain products or services to you. We will advise you if this is the case at the time you withdraw your consent.

       7. **International Transfers.** WindBorne is based in the United States, and we and our service providers may process personal information in the United States and other countries whose data protection laws may differ from those where you live. Where applicable law requires safeguards for an international transfer, we use legally recognized mechanisms, such as adequacy decisions or contractual protections. You may contact us for more information about the safeguards that apply to your personal information.


06. ### RETENTION OF INFORMATION.


    Subject to your right to request deletion of your personal information, we will retain your personal information as long as needed for your use of the Services, your approved receipt of marketing communications from us, our compliance with legal obligations, and to protect our or others’ interests. We retain personal information associated with AI Weather Tool requests, analytics, and technical logs only for as long as reasonably necessary to provide, secure, monitor, troubleshoot, and improve the Services and comply with applicable law. The applicable period depends on whether the information remains linked or reasonably linkable to a user or session, the sensitivity of the information, and the operational purpose for which it is retained. We may retain aggregated or de-identified information that can no longer reasonably be linked to an individual for longer periods.


    **Website submissions and correspondence.** We retain website submissions and correspondence in the relevant form-processing, internal operations, and email systems as reasonably needed to handle the request, complete related recovery or community-launch activities, manage an ongoing relationship, resolve disputes, or meet legal obligations. The retention period depends on those purposes and the nature of the request.

07. ### BROWSER PRIVACY SIGNALS.


    The new marketing website does not currently change its behavior in response to the legacy Do Not Track browser setting. That setting is distinct from legally recognized opt-out preference signals, such as Global Privacy Control, which can convey an opt-out of the sale or sharing of personal information where applicable law provides that right. This statement about legacy Do Not Track does not limit rights you have under applicable law. To ask about our handling of your information or exercise your privacy rights, contact [contact@windbornesystems.com](mailto:contact@windbornesystems.com). External providers may separately collect information about your activity when their content is loaded, as described above.

08. ### AGE OF USERS.


    The Services are not directed to children under 13 or any higher minimum age required by applicable law, and the AI Weather Tools may be accessed only by users who meet the age requirements of the applicable third-party artificial intelligence service. We do not knowingly collect or solicit information from anyone below the applicable minimum age. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a child below the applicable minimum age, we will delete that information as quickly as possible.

09. ### CHANGES TO POLICY.


    We may update this Policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we will post the updated Policy and revise the effective date above. We will provide additional notice or obtain consent where required by applicable law.

10. ### CONTACT US.


    If you have any questions or concerns regarding this Policy, please send us a detailed message to [contact@windbornesystems.com](mailto:contact@windbornesystems.com?subject=Question%20Regarding%20WindBorne%20Privacy%20Policy), and we will try to resolve your concerns.


## Cookie Policy

Effective Date: October 22, 2026

This Cookie Policy explains cookies and related technologies used in connection with the Services described in our [Privacy Policy](https://windbornesystems.com/ext/legal#privacy-policy). Their use varies between the public marketing website, account-based products, and external content providers.

### What is a Cookie?

A cookie is a small text file stored on and accessed from your device. Cookies and related technologies, such as browser storage and pixels, can support authentication, preferences, content delivery, analytics, and advertising. Not every Service uses every type of technology described here.

### How to Manage Cookies and Embedded Content

Change cookie preferences

On the marketing website, Accept enables optional analytics and Reject leaves it off. Use “Change cookie preferences” above to change your choice. We remember either choice in browser storage for six calendar months; visiting again does not extend that period. If you withdraw permission, we stop website analytics and clear its Google Analytics cookies. Clearing site data, using a different browser, or reaching the expiry date may prompt a new choice. Browser Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track signals keep website analytics off. You can also use your browser settings to block or delete cookies and manage other site data. Blocking some cookies may prevent features, such as account sign-in, from working. Where embedded media displays an “Allow and load” notice, you can leave it unloaded or choose to load that individual item. “Unload” removes it from the page but does not clear existing cookies or erase information already received by the provider. Our Luma event calendar loads automatically rather than using these per-embed controls. Provider privacy links explain their practices and available choices.

### Types of Cookies

The following categories describe how cookies can work; they are not a statement that every category is used on every page.

- First-party cookies are set by the site you visit. Third-party cookies are set by external providers.

- Session cookies expire at the end of a browser session. Persistent cookies remain until they expire or you delete them.

- Necessary cookies support core functions, such as login and authentication.

- Functionality cookies remember choices or preferences where those features are offered.

- Analytics cookies help measure usage and performance.

- Marketing cookies can support advertising and measure or personalize ads. External media and social providers may use these technologies when their content is loaded.


### First-Party Cookies

Services that provide account sign-in use necessary cookies for login and authentication. These account features are separate from browsing the public marketing pages or submitting a contact form.

### External Providers

Media and social providers, including YouTube, Vimeo, LinkedIn, SoundCloud, and CBS News, may use cookies or device storage when you enable their embedded content. Their individual notices link to their privacy policies. The Luma calendar loads automatically and may use cookies and analytics technologies; see [Luma’s Privacy Policy](https://luma.com/privacy-policy).
